question: Should OpenClaw make AI-safety events a public plugin SDK subscription/emission contract with durable shared-state history, or keep the first version internal to core diagnostics/exporters until authority, retention, and upgrade semantics are designed?
rationale: This choice establishes a new external plugin contract, subscriber authorization model, and persistent operator-data surface; code review cannot safely infer the intended long-term product boundary.

options.title: Approve a narrow core contract
options.body: Define authorized emitters and subscribers, the stable event schema, retention/privacy policy, and a tested supported upgrade path before completing this PR.

options.title: Keep the first phase internal
options.body: Limit the work to core-owned diagnostic/exporter hooks and defer public plugin emission, subscription, UI, and durable-query APIs until a separate SDK design is approved.

options.title: Route extensibility outside core
options.body: Keep generic core diagnostics only and require optional safety collectors and dashboards to use a plugin/ClawHub package once an adequate generic seam exists.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Define authorized emitters and subscribers, the stable event schema, retention/privacy policy, and a tested supported upgrade path before completing this PR.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the documented proposer and author of the cross-cutting design, so they are best positioned to clarify the intended initial boundary with a repository owner.
